how: We read the website of every Austin wedding photographer listed on Lazo (95 listings, 79 sites reachable) and set aside the ones that are not really in the wedding business: corporate event and headshot photographers, a booking marketplace, a multi-service franchise, a venue blog post standing in for a site, and a photographer whose page says San Francisco. What is left is a shortlist of vendors who say clearly what they do, show their work, and tell you how they work. Verified Lazo vendors come first. Nobody paid to be here, and this is not a ranking: Lazo ranks only on reviews from couples who booked.
ask: How do you handle a July ceremony in direct sun, and do you plan portraits around the Hill Country sunset?
Can I see a full gallery from one wedding at a venue like mine, not just the highlights?
What is the delivery timeline, and is a second shooter included or an add-on?

picks.name: Alexandra Joy Wedding Photography
picks.blurb: Alexandra Joy has crafted wedding photos for more than 12 years, blending candid storytelling with an elegant, editorial approach. After photographing over 400 weddings in Toronto she has brought the work to Austin, serving Dripping Springs and the Hill Country from Leander.

picks.name: Bhuvana Dhinesh Photography
picks.blurb: A South Asian wedding photographer based in Texas who specializes in Indian, fusion and destination weddings. Since 2017 Bhuvana Dhinesh has documented multi-day celebrations from haldi and mehendi through sangeet, pheras and nikah, with images meant to feel artful and personal. Based in Liberty Hill.

picks.name: Stephanie Rogers Photography
picks.blurb: Bradley and Stephanie Rogers are a husband-and-wife Austin team, established in 2014, making candid photos for couples who would rather feel it than fake it. Their pitch is that a photographer should understand who you actually are as a couple, and everyone is welcome.

picks.name: Thirdeyestudio
picks.blurb: Thirdeyestudio is an Austin-based collective of photographers and filmmakers founded by PV Subramanian in 2009, shooting Indian, Pakistani and fusion weddings in a documentary way. Engagement shoots start at $749 for two hours and wedding quotes are built custom around hours and outputs.

picks.name: Ryan Green Photography
picks.blurb: Ryan and Lindsey Green are Austin wedding photographers who say they love photography as much as their city, with a stated passion for prime lenses, afternoon light and good breakfast tacos. Ryan's start was his father's darkroom in the family garage.

picks.name: Matt Montalvo Photography
picks.blurb: Matt Montalvo has documented more than 1,000 weddings since 2007 and shoots 55 to 70 a year, enough to have seen nearly every way a day can unfold. Unlike bigger studios, he personally shoots, edits and delivers every image himself, based in Austin and traveling for destination weddings.

picks.name: Caitlin McWeeney Photography
picks.blurb: Caitlin McWeeney has photographed colorful, candid, true-to-life Austin weddings since 2011 and makes the case for hiring a full-time wedding photographer, which she is. A self-described people person whose favorite moment is when a couple stops thinking about the camera.

picks.name: Bonnie Burke Weddings
picks.blurb: Bonnie Burke is an inclusive documentary wedding photographer in Austin who shoots digital, film and Super 8, with a photojournalistic approach and an editorial bent. 2025 marks her fifteenth year as a photographer, and her first rule is that your wedding day is not a photoshoot.

picks.name: Jenny DeMarco Photography
picks.blurb: Jenny DeMarco has photographed weddings for more than fifteen years across Texas, the U.S. and abroad, with work rooted in documentary photography and a strong eye for design and fashion. Her site notes features in The New York Times and Martha Stewart, and she covers Austin, Houston, Dallas and San Antonio.

picks.name: Technicolor Weddings
picks.blurb: Technicolor Weddings is Bill McCullough, a photographer and musician, and Meredith, a printmaker and bookbinder, who approach weddings as working artists: no staging, no acting. Bill pioneered the nontraditional style 22 years ago, and the studio offers handmade wedding books.

picks.name: Amanda Lynn Photography
picks.blurb: Amanda Lynn Williams moved to Texas from Tennessee in 2020 and calls herself your ultimate hype gal. Her Leander studio prints its pricing: wedding coverage starts at $3,000, destination weddings from $2,000 plus travel, and every wedding package includes a complimentary engagement session.

picks.name: Pink Salt Pics
picks.blurb: Formerly Lori Blythe Photography, Pink Salt Pics is the same photographer under a new name, now based in Dripping Springs and shooting Fredericksburg and Austin as well. She offers four customizable wedding collections and a mini video add-on, in a style she describes as classic, clean and emotion-driven.
